director.chapterArc: A pivot from survival against monsters to preparation for human deception, marked by Rook's tactical shift and his admission of error.
director.restraintNote: Maintain a grounded, observational tone throughout. The horror lies in the clinical description of new tactics; do not dramatize the training or Bram Stell's revelation with emotional inflection beyond factual weight.

cues.delivery: Toren's sensory shift from enclosed hedge to open sky; a physical recoil felt through pacing.
cues.from: Toren had been watching the hedges. There had been two of them for eleven miles, one on each hand, gone up into trees and grown together overhead in places, and for four days they had been the whole world. Then the left one stopped. Then the right one stopped. The lane came out of the tunnel it had been into a flat open place with a sky on it, and the sky was so large and so gray and so entirely without cover that Toren's shoulders came up around his ears before he knew he had done it.
cues.through: Toren had been watching the hedges. There had been two of them for eleven miles, one on each hand, gone up into trees and grown together overhead in places, and for four days they had been the whole world. Then the left one stopped. Then the right one stopped. The lane came out of the tunnel it had been into a flat open place with a sky on it, and the sky was so large and so gray and so entirely without cover that Toren's shoulders came up around his ears before he knew he had done it.
cues.reason: Establish the environmental change that triggers Toren's anxiety.

cues.delivery: Rook's rare praise; flat and precise to contrast with the group's exhaustion.
cues.from: "Good," Rook said. "That's the first thing any of you have done this week that I'd have paid money for."
cues.through: "Good," Rook said. "That's the first thing any of you have done this week that I'd have paid money for."
cues.reason: Highlight Rook's approval as a tactical marker rather than emotional validation.

cues.delivery: Senna's exposition; dry and authoritative, establishing her age as a source of knowledge.
cues.from: "Wayhouse," said Senna, from the cart, with her eyes shut. "Or it was. There'll have been a trade in that once. Beer and a floor and a byre, and you paid by the head of stock, not by the man."
cues.through: "Because I am extremely old, Milo, and because there's a trough out there you could water thirty beasts at. Nobody cuts that much stone for a house."
cues.reason: Differentiate Senna's voice through factual weight without melodrama.

cues.delivery: Rook's tactical briefing; clipped and rhythmic, emphasizing the 'why' for Toren.
cues.from: "Eighty yards," he said. "All of you, off the road, on the pinfold wall where you can be seen and can't be reached. Wyck stays on the cart. Dessa, you're calling. Milo, hands where they show. Toren, with me and one step behind."
cues.through: "Because you're the one who's been asking me questions for a fortnight," Rook said, "and I'd rather you got a look at where the answers come from."
cues.reason: Establish Rook as a teacher of specific mechanics rather than general advice.

cues.delivery: Bram Stell's interrogation; flat and hurried, reflecting his isolation.
cues.from: "Nobody comes off the ridge lane." The billhook did not move. "That's eleven miles of nothing and it's been that since I was a boy. A man who takes it with a cart is a man who doesn't want to be on the Marl. What's behind you?"
cues.reason: Convey the tension of a man who has been waiting to speak for days.

cues.delivery: Bram's revelation of the brass coin; a shift from factual to suspicious.
cues.from: "Nine." Bram Stell said it immediately. He had been waiting five days to be asked. "Nine, and two of them women, and every one of them fed. That's the thing I keep going back to. They were fed. You don't see fed people on this road."
cues.through: "Coin. Real coin, four bits of it, station-struck, and one bit of brass that isn't money." The old man's mouth went sideways. "I asked about the brass. The one doing the talking said it was better than money on the right road, and to keep it, and not to be too quick about showing it to anybody."
cues.reason: Mark the transition from general description to specific threat intelligence.

cues.delivery: Rook's retraction; a rare moment of self-correction delivered with absolute flatness.
cues.through: It was the only time in twenty-five days that Toren had heard him take one back.
cues.reason: Emphasize the significance of Rook admitting error without vocalizing it.

cues.delivery: The exchange about 'who else keeps a book'; the weight of the question lands in silence.
cues.from: "She asked me who else keeps a book."
cues.through: "Water's clean," he said at last. "Take what you want of it."
cues.reason: Let the implication of the list hang without over-acting Bram's fear.

cues.delivery: Rook's pivot to human tactics; a shift from monster mechanics to psychological warfare.
cues.from: "Right," he said. "Everything I have taught the four of you for twenty-five days has been about a thing that cannot change its mind."
cues.through: "Because the road's got people on it," Rook said, "and the ridge lane hasn't got anything on it at all, and we've come off the one and onto the other."
cues.reason: Signal the thematic turn of the chapter through pacing and clarity.

cues.delivery: The instruction to throw at a face; clinical acceptance of violence as necessity.
cues.reason: Maintain the detached tone required for this brutal tactical lesson.

cues.delivery: Rook's instruction to Wyck on being a 'door'; the shift from static defense to dynamic positioning.
cues.from: "You I'm going to tell the worst one," Rook said.
cues.through: "He did, and it was the best thing anybody did that day. He'll get it wrong nine times out of the next ten. So will you." Rook picked up the hazel rod at last. "That's the lesson. Everybody up. We're going to do the stop-and-close on a person for twenty minutes and then we're going to stop, because you'll all be worse at everything tomorrow if we don't."
cues.reason: Clarify the tactical distinction between wall and door without emotional flourish.

cues.delivery: The drill's failure; Toren's realization of the human threat through physical proximity.
cues.from: They did it for twenty minutes and it was horrible.
cues.through: "Good," he said. "That's enough of that for one evening."
cues.reason: Convey the horror of the training exercise through stillness and observation.

cues.delivery: Toren's internal arithmetic; the cold calculation of numbers and unanswered questions.
cues.from: Nine men, fed, coming up from the east. Coin and a piece of brass that was not money. A book bought at eleven times its worth by a woman who held it in both hands and said thank you.
cues.through: Nobody said it. That was the part Toren could not get past, lying down at last with the fire a seam and a wall at his back. Five people had spent an evening learning where to hit a man in the face, and not one of them had asked which man.
cues.reason: Reflect Toren's analytical mind processing the group's vulnerability.

pauses.after: Toren had not seen washing on a line since Hobb's Wall.
pauses.reason: Completed thought on washing line; pause for Toren's memory association.
Emphasis on the specific type of traveler to establish Bram's suspicion.

pauses.after: The old man's face did not do anything at all for about two seconds.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing: the old man's reaction to 'Coldharbour' being gone.
Isolate the name as a critical piece of intelligence regarding Coldharbour.
Emphasize the anomaly of 'fed' people to highlight their danger.

The one doing the talking said it was better than money on the right road, and to keep it, and not to be too quick about showing it to anybody."

Major emotional landing: Rook retracting his question; a rare moment of vulnerability.

pauses.after: "She asked me who else keeps a book."
pauses.reason: Completed thought on the book list; pause for the weight of the implication.

pauses.before: She asked me who else keeps a book.
pauses.reason: Isolate the pivotal question that drives the chapter's tension.

pauses.after: "It's not an answer. It's the only true thing I've got and I'm not going to improve it for you." Rook shouldered his pack. "How far to Wenn's Ford on the north road?"
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing: Rook's reassurance to Bram Stell about his job being done.
Emphasize the limitation of monsters to set up Rook's new lesson.

pauses.after: "A Husk has one plan. A verge-hound has one plan; it picks that plan early and cannot re-pick it. A stilt has a line and a stop, and the stop is the whole of your business. All of that is true. None of it is going anywhere. We're going to keep drilling it until you're bored." He let that sit for a second. "And it is all completely useless against a man."
pauses.reason: Scene break; pause for the shift from monster tactics to human deception training.

pauses.after: That was an answer. Toren thought about it for the rest of the evening and could not find a single thing in it that was a lie, and could not find the part of it that was true either.
pauses.reason: Completed thought on Rook's answer; allow Toren's internal processing time.
Clarify the tactical shift from conversation to manipulation.
Isolate the brutal instruction as a key learning point for Milo.
Major emotional landing: The acceptance of the 'rotten thing' as necessary training.

pauses.reason: Emphasize the specific scenario to contrast with monster behavior.

Speaker reset; pause after Rook's command to repeat the drill.

pauses.reason: Completed thought on Dessa not speaking; pause for Toren's realization of silence.
